title: introduce-geozone-policy-compiler-and-audit-anchoring-for-kms-usage
author: Maya Chen
description:
Context: Customers have asked for a single declarative way to express data residency boundaries that automatically produce enforcement artifacts for RBAC v2, KMS key selection policies, and immutable audit anchors. This PR adds a lightweight "geozone policy compiler" that compiles high-level residency rules into RBAC role bindings, KMS key usage constraints (key-metadata predicates), and an audit anchoring proxy that signs and pins audit records with region assertions.
Motivation: Reduce operator error when translating residency requirements into runtime policies, eliminate drift between KMS scoping and RBAC, and provide cryptographically verifiable audit anchors that show which region assertion was used to authorize a request.
What this PR does: 1) New policy compiler service (pkg/policy/compiler) that accepts a small YAML/JSON DSL describing geozone rules (geozone id, tenants, allowed key regions, enforcement mode). 2) Compiler emits: a) RBAC v2 Role + RoleBinding templates with attribute constraints (attribute matcher on tenant.region, tenant.kms_origin); b) KMS policy metadata annotations used by key-router to prefer/deny keys; c) Audit anchor forwarder (services/audit/anchor) that signs a compact provenance envelope and attaches "geozone-assertion" headers to audit logs. 3) A validation CLI (tools/policy-validate) for CI to lint geozone files and fail PRs on dangerous open rules. 4) Migration helper that converts legacy tenant-scoped kms annotations into the new geozone DSL for rollout.
Design notes: - Compiler is intentionally hermetic and returns only declarative artifacts; it does not apply bindings directly to clusters. Application of compiled artifacts is handled by the existing rbactooling pipeline so we can gate rollout. - Audit anchor uses existing signing key infrastructure (KMS-wrapped local sig keys) and produces an envelope with canonicalized policy hash to prevent later tampering. - Enforcement modes: audit-only | enforce | soft-enforce (logs + throttle) to allow staged rollout.
Compatibility: Backwards-compatible with current RBAC v2 runtime; existing Role/Binding names are preserved when migrating using the helper. KMS router will accept new key-metadata annotations but falls back to old behavior when annotations missing.
Testing: Unit tests for compiler, E2E test harness that runs a local rbactooling apply step, and a small integration test exercising the audit anchor verification path (tests/integration/audit-anchor). All tests added; coverage gate + CI lint.
Rollout plan: 1) Merge as opt-in feature behind feature flag (feature.geozone_compiler=false by default). 2) Run validation CLI in policy repos and migrate two pilot tenants. 3) Switch enforcement mode to soft-enforce for 2 weeks, monitor metrics (rbac.denied_by_geozone, audit.anchor_failures). 4) Flip to enforce after signoff.
Security review: SEC-78 ticket covers threat modelling; key points addressed: no plaintext key material emitted, audit anchor envelopes are signed and include policy hash, compiled RBAC artifacts include attribute matchers (not broad role grants).
References: Linear ENG-2034, ticket SEC-78, design doc: docs/design/geozone-policy-compiler.md

review_comments: Diego Morales: Can we make the compiled RBAC names stable to avoid churn when re-compiling? Suggest using hashed suffix with tenant+geozone so names are deterministic.
Maya Chen (author): Good call — implemented deterministic name strategy using sha256(tenant|geozone) and documented it in README.
Aisha Patel: Audit envelope looks good; add a compact JSON-LD context so downstream verifiers can reason about schema versioning.
Maya Chen (author): Added context and bumped envelope schema to v1.1 in anchor.go.
Jonah Park: Policy-validate needs to fail loudly on 'allow-all' catch-alls; unit test covers this but CI job was flaky, please re-run.
Maya Chen (author): Fixed race in validation test and re-triggered CI; removed flaky temp file usage.
Security (automated): Static analysis flagged potential nil deref in compiler when key-metadata absent — added defensive checks and unit test.

release_notes: Added a geozone policy compiler that emits RBAC v2 bindings, KMS metadata annotations, and an audit anchoring proxy. Feature is behind feature flag and includes a validation CLI for CI. See docs/design/geozone-policy-compiler.md for migration steps.
